title: {{ORG_NAME}} AI Governance Manifest
description: Authoritative per-asset metadata. One home per question: this manifest is the source; AWS resource tags and GitHub topics are projections of it. Field requirements below describe the Tier 2+ shape (MUST). For Tier 1, a manifest is recommended (SHOULD) and only asset_id, name, version, workload_type, and owner are expected.

asset_id.$comment: SUBSTITUTION REQUIRED: replace {{ASSET_ID_PREFIX}} in the pattern above with the adopter's literal prefix (default ORG-AI-) before this schema will validate any asset_id. JSON carries no comments, so this note lives here.

name.description: Lowercase repo/asset slug. No invented abbreviations.

scope.description: This standard governs non-product AI. Product is governed separately.

workload_type.description: Structural axis. Classify by dependency position, not implementation.

tier.description: B1.3 — worse of potential harm and degree of independence.

owner.description: Solution Owner (Accountable). A person, not a team.

business_unit.description: Owning domain — the business unit or functional area (the <domain> slot). No abbreviations.

vendor.description: Platform the asset targets or runs on (the <vendor> slot): aws, snowflake, aiven, claude, github, workato, etc.

environment.description: Deployment-time value. Belongs in the manifest and AWS tags, never in a public GitHub topic.

records.description: Governed records. Requirements approved at Gate 1; Epic opened at Gate 1 before build (B1.9); Spec added during build and required before the pre-flight gate (B1.7).

requirements.description: Link to approved AI Solution Requirements.

spec.description: Link to Solution Spec. Required before pre-flight (B1.7).

epic.description: Work-tracker Epic key (Jira in the reference configuration) (B1.9).

mcp_servers.description: MCP servers/connectors the asset reaches. Feeds the AIBOM (SDLC Build stage) and connector review.
